name: Broadband home move
blurb: Vague date, changes her mind twice
title: Moving the service to a new house with a vague date and two changes of mind
summary: A Belfast caller moving house says only 'the end of the month', corrects the date mid-sentence and pauses inside the new address. She then moves the install to the Monday and moves it back again. If the agent guesses the date, keeps the day she dropped or gets the postcode wrong, she corrects it, and gives up if it happens again.

golden.scenario: Caller is moving house at the end of August and wants broadband moved to the new address.
golden.expected_outcome: The agent asks which date she means instead of assuming the 31st. The home move is booked to 27 Cregagh Gardens, Belfast, BT6 9EQ. The install is on Saturday 29 August in the afternoon, not Friday the 28th and not Monday the 31st. The agent says the old address is disconnected the same day.

agent_setup.policy: The old address is disconnected on the day the new one is installed. No charge for a home move.

nodes.say: End of the month, like I said.
Hold on, I never said the thirty-first. Ask me, don't be guessin'.
We get the keys on Friday the twenty-eighth. No, sorry, that's the old plan. Saturday the twenty-ninth.
No, not the Friday. Saturday. Saturday the twenty-ninth.
It's twenty-seven Cregagh Gardens, Belfast, B T six, nine E Q.
No. Twenty-seven. Cregagh, C, R, E, G, A, G, H. B T six, nine E Q.
Wait, actually, no. My fella's workin' the Saturday. Can ye make it the Monday instead? The thirty-first, mornin'.
Och, d'you know what, leave it the Saturday afternoon after all. My ma can let them in.
No! I said go back to the Saturday. Saturday the twenty-ninth, afternoon.
And when does the old house get cut off? I'm not payin' for the two of them.
That's grand. Thanks a million, bye.
Ach, forget it. I'll do it in the shop.
